perf.summary: math.distance computes a sqrt every edge; document/expose that cost cannot avoid it but ensure areaCost lookup is the only added work.
perf.currentCost: GetCost = math.distance(pa,pb) * areaCost[curPoly->GetArea()]. math.distance performs a length (sqrt) per call; this runs once per traversed edge during A* expansion, so it is genuinely hot.
perf.proposedChange: Keep math.distance (the cost model requires true Euclidean length, not squared), but confirm GetArea() is a cheap masked field read and consider caching curPoly->GetArea() result if GetCost is called alongside other GetArea() reads in the caller. No change to this method beyond verifying AggressiveInlining (already present).
perf.rationale: The sqrt is semantically required (path cost must be additive linear distance), so it cannot be strength-reduced without changing results. The only safe win is ensuring the area lookup and inlining are optimal, which they already are.
perf.risk: Replacing distance with lengthsq would change cost semantics (non-additive), so it is rejected. No safe cycle reduction exists here - reported as already near-optimal.
